extracted.intended_audience: NRSA/NIH predoctoral fellowship applicants, fellowship reviewers, mentors
extracted.subtask_description: An NRSA-format predoctoral fellowship research strategy and training plan describing experimental approaches, preliminary data, mentorship, responsible conduct training, facilities, and sponsor/co-sponsor statements. Intended to justify the feasibility, rigor, and training environment for a predoctoral fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Approach — Crystallization and structure determination
rubrics_metrics.description: We have obtained initial crystals from 96-well screens for both the “non-activating” and “hyper-activating” dsRNA complexes with OAS1 that diffract to medium resolution (~7 Å). I will next optimize these crystals using additional screens around the initial conditions, adjusting parameters such as the concentrations of OAS1-dsRNA complex, salt, or precipitant, pH, and temperature. If needed, I will also test detergents and other additives to improve crystal formation. Diffraction data sets will be collected at the SER-CAT beamline at the APS. Once suitable quality data are obtained, I will determine the structure by molecular replacement using the structure of RNA-bound OAS1 (PDB 4IG8) as a starting model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes concrete experimental steps (optimization variables: protein/RNA concentration, salt, precipitant, pH, temperature, additives), data collection location (SER-CAT/APS), and intended structure solution method (molecular replacement using PDB 4IG8). Also lists available software (HKL2000, Phenix, Coot) for processing, refinement, and model building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Analysis / Rigor — Structure validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures will be validated during refinement with Phenix, and I will use the Protein Data Bank (PDB) server to ensure our data and final structures are of optimal quality prior to deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit plan to use established software (Phenix) for validation during refinement and to check with PDB validation tools prior to finalizing structures; implies adherence to community standards for structure quality and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data Demonstrating Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot experiments demonstrate potential for acquiring high quality HDX-MS data (100% coverage, 33-fold redundancy). Crystals were shown to contain both RNA and protein and diffraction from a crystal extends to at least 7 Å. Deuterium uptake from a pilot exchange experiment shows that RNA-induced changes can be monitored by this method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides quantitative pilot metrics (coverage, redundancy, diffraction limit) and an explicit demonstration that chosen methods can detect the expected biological signal; used to justify feasibility of approaches (HDX-MS, crystallography).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and Interpretation — Linking structures to hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures of the OAS1-dsRNA complexes will reveal the molecular details underpinning the differing ability of each dsRNA to activate OAS1. These structures will provide a detailed platform for interpretation of findings in other subaims as well as allowing me to develop and test (by mutagenesis and functional assays) new hypotheses about critical OAS1-dsRNA interactions for potent activation or for dsRNA binding in the absence of OAS1 activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how structural outcomes will be interpreted and used to generate and test mechanistic hypotheses (mutagenesis, functional assays), demonstrating a clear plan for downstream use of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Pitfalls and Alternative Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: My preliminary data indicate BLI will be applicable to OAS-dsRNA binding affinity/kinetics but, if needed, other approaches are well established in our lab and several options are available (e.g., surface plasmon resonance or isothermal titration calorimetry in the Emory Comprehensive Glycomics core). I also do not anticipate technical issues with HDX-MS as our preliminary data clearly support the feasibility of this approach. Finally, X-ray crystallography is inherently full of potential pitfalls but progress in obtaining diffracting crystals of both complexes and our lab’s track record in structure determination give strong cause for optimism that I will obtain high-resolution structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies risks for each technique and names concrete alternative methods/cores; uses lab track record and pilot results to mitigate perceived risks. Demonstrates awareness of method-specific pitfalls and contingency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respective Contributions and Candidate Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary data presented in this proposal was collected and analyzed by me unless otherwise specifically noted in the corresponding figure legend. Moving forward, for the experiments described in this proposal, I will design, conduct, analyze, and interpret the results with assistance from Drs. Conn and Lowen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which work is the candidate's own, and defines the candidate's primary responsibilities (design, execution, analysis, interpretation) while acknowledging mentorship and assistance; important for demonstrating independence and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Sponsor and Institution — Rationale and Training Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: BCDB offers attractive training opportunities (Foundations, seminar courses, a second-year scientific writing course using an NRSA-style format), yearly retreats, methods and professionalization workshops, and a guaranteed stipend. The program's collaborative and supportive environment, institutional core facilities, and the broader Emory research environment provide resources needed to perform cutting-edge research and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why the chosen program/institution is well suited to support the candidate's training: courses, workshops, mentorship culture, core facilities, and financial support; demonstrates institutional fit and access to necessary resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) Training
rubrics_metrics.description: All Emory University graduate students are required to take a six-hour ethics seminar course (Jones Program in Ethics, JPE 600) and attend at least four additional workshops sponsored by the Laney Graduate School or the Emory Center for Ethics. The BCDB program requires monthly one-hour ethics workshops (eight per school year) with specific topics (Conflict of Interest; Animal Experiments and IACUC; Human Subjects and Tissues; Mentor-Mentee Responsibilities; Collaborative Research; Peer Review; Data Management and Sharing; Research Misconduct and Data Manipulation; Responsible Authorship and Publication). The requirement meets the NIH requirement for retraining every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concrete RCR training plan that lists required courses, workshop frequency, specific topics covered, faculty involvement, and compliance with NIH retraining expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Plan — Co-mentorship and Mentor Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Samantha (Sam) Schwartz will be co-mentored by Dr. Graeme L. Conn (expertise in RNA structure and RNA-protein interactions) and Dr. Anice Lowen (expertise in molecular virology and cell culture systems). The sponsors provide complementary perspectives and mentoring experience relevant to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes complementary expertise of sponsor and co-sponsor and how co-mentorship will provide both technical and career guidance; demonstrates an intentional mentorship structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in Diverse Experimental Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: The project will employ diverse approaches that will provide new training in biochemical (OAS1 enzyme kinetics), structural (x-ray crystallography) and other biophysical approaches (BLI and HDX-MS). The use of cell culture approaches in Dr. Lowen’s lab will further broaden technical training and provide biological context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies multiple complementary technical skills the candidate will gain, showing breadth of technical training and increased impact of findings through biological validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship Meetings — One-on-one Frequency and Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary mentor's door is open; candidate meets with mentor informally 3-4 times a week and, when greater input is needed, meetings are scheduled at least once a week. Dr. Lowen will begin meeting regularly with the candidate once cell-culture-based aspects commence. Meetings will include discussion of experimental plans, interpretation, record-keeping, analysis, and manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies frequency and modes of mentor–trainee interaction (informal frequent check-ins plus scheduled weekly meetings during critical phases), showing active mentorship and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly Laboratory Meetings — Presentation and Peer Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The lab holds weekly joint meetings with Dr. Christine Dunham’s group; one member typically presents latest results or a recent paper. Meetings are used to practice formal presentations of a more complete 'story' prior to conferences or manuscript submission. Dr. Lowen's group attends when the candidate presents, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates ongoing, structured opportunities for practice, critique, and iterative improvement of presentations and data interpretation via regular group meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentations and Conference Attendance — Professional Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate is encouraged to present early and often: BCDB introductory and advanced seminars, joint lab meetings, Emory RNA Club, DSAC symposium (poster and later podium), regional meetings (SERVC), and national meetings (RNA Society, ASM, ASBMB). Candidate will be encouraged to attend at least one scientific meeting per year and to apply for travel awards; training courses in macromolecular crystallography are also recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies targets and timeline for presentation opportunities, expectation of at least annual conference attendance, available funding sources (Laney PDS funds, lab funds), and support for applying to travel fellowships; highlights explicit professional development plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis Committee — Composition and Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Thesis committee comprises sponsor, co-sponsor, and three department faculty with diverse expertise (structural biology, RNA biology, biochemistry). The committee will meet for 1–2 hours every six months as dictated by the BCDB program, and the candidate will meet individually with committee members as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides committee composition and regular semiannual review schedule for progress oversight and guidance, ensuring structured external input into training and research direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Record-Keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate piloted the use of an electronic notebook (Findings) allowing sharing of protocols and experimental results via Emory Box. This approach allows the mentor to track progress with experiments, offer immediate input on record keeping, analysis, interpretation and prepare for meetings with better insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies electronic record-keeping tools and shared platforms to support reproducibility, oversight, and collaborative analysis; indicates an explicit data-management practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor/Co-sponsor Mentorship Record and Trainee Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor (Conn) and Co-sponsor (Lowen) list previous and current pre- and post-doctoral trainees, with representative former trainees and current positions (academic and industry). Mentors describe their history of mentoring, roles in graduate programs, and involvement in training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses concrete trainee records and mentor involvement in training programs to document mentors' experience and capacity for trainee development; relevant for assessing mentorship quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support and Institutional Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists current and pending grants (e.g., R01 AI088025-07 and others) with direct $/yr amounts and notes availability of institutional core facilities (SER-CAT beamline at the APS, Emory Comprehensive Glycomics core) to support the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates availability of financial support and specialized facilities/cores necessary to complete the proposed research; supports feasibility and resource adequacy.
